title: New Australian Study Investigates Rising Health Issues in Younger People
subtitle: Researchers are tracking 100,000 people to understand why mental health problems and early-onset cancers are increasing.

summary.en: A new research project called '18 and Up' has launched in Australia to study the long-term health of young adults. The study aims to collect data from 100,000 participants aged 18 to 45. Researchers want to understand why mental health disorders are becoming more common in this age group. The project will also investigate the reasons behind the global rise in early-onset cancers. By following participants over many years, scientists hope to improve future health systems and prevention strategies.
summary.zh: 澳洲啟動了一項名為「18歲及以上」的新研究計畫，旨在探討年輕成人的長期健康狀況。該研究目標是收集十萬名18至45歲參與者的數據。研究人員希望了解為何心理健康障礙在該年齡層變得愈發普遍，並將調查全球早發性癌症增加背後的原因。透過長達多年的追蹤，科學家期望能藉此改善未來的健康體系與預防策略。

paragraphs.en: A major new health study is starting in Australia to help experts understand the growing health challenges facing younger generations. The project, named '18 and Up,' aims to follow the lives of 100,000 people between the ages of 18 and 45. According to The Guardian, this is the largest study of its kind in the country, and it hopes to find answers to why mental health problems and certain types of cancer are becoming more common among young adults.
paragraphs.zh: 澳洲正展開一項大型的新健康研究，旨在協助專家了解年輕世代所面臨日益嚴峻的健康挑戰。這項名為「18歲及以上」（18 and Up）的計畫，目標是追蹤十萬名年齡介於18至45歲民眾的生活。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，這是該國同類型研究中規模最大的一項，研究人員希望藉此找出為何心理健康問題與特定癌症在年輕成人族群中變得愈發普遍的原因。

paragraphs.en: The study is led by the Sax Institute, a non-profit research organization. This group has a long history of health research; two decades ago, they started a similar project called '45 and Up,' which tracks the health of older Australians. The new study will build on this experience by looking at how health changes over a person's entire life. By inviting the children and grandchildren of the original participants to join, researchers hope to see how family history, life experiences, and social conditions work together to affect health across different generations.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究由非營利研究機構「薩克斯研究所」（Sax Institute）主導。該機構在健康研究領域擁有悠久歷史；二十年前，他們曾發起一項名為「45歲及以上」（45 and Up）的類似計畫，用於追蹤澳洲年長者的健康狀況。這項新研究將奠基於過往經驗，探討健康如何隨著人的一生而改變。透過邀請最初參與者的子女與孫輩加入，研究人員希望能觀察家庭背景、生活經驗與社會條件如何共同影響不同世代的健康。

paragraphs.en: One of the main goals of the study is to address the rise in mental health disorders. According to The Guardian, nearly two out of every five young Australians aged 16 to 24 experienced a mental health problem in the past year. Adjunct Professor Justine Gatt, the scientific director of the study, noted that these numbers have been rising, but there is not enough long-term evidence to explain why. Because suicide is the leading cause of death for Australians aged 15 to 44, researchers believe it is urgent to understand these factors to create better prevention programs and treatments.
paragraphs.zh: 該研究的主要目標之一是解決心理健康障礙增加的問題。根據《衛報》報導，在過去一年中，每五名16至24歲的澳洲年輕人裡，就有近兩人經歷過心理健康問題。該研究的科學總監、兼任教授賈斯汀·蓋特（Justine Gatt）指出，這些數據一直在上升，但目前缺乏足夠的長期證據來解釋原因。由於自殺是澳洲15至44歲人口的主要死因，研究人員認為，了解這些因素對於制定更完善的預防計畫與治療方案刻不容緩。

paragraphs.en: In addition to mental health, the study will look closely at the rise of early-onset cancers. These are cancers diagnosed in people who are older than teenagers but younger than 50. The Guardian reports that cases of bowel, thyroid, and breast cancer have been increasing in this age group since the year 2000, both in Australia and in other parts of the world. While scientists have some ideas about why this is happening, they still need more information. Potential causes include changes in modern lifestyles, different types of environmental exposures during childhood, and the effects of increased medical screening.
paragraphs.zh: 除了心理健康外，研究也將密切關注早發性癌症的增加。這類癌症是指在青少年之後、50歲以前被診斷出的癌症。《衛報》報導指出，自2000年以來，無論是在澳洲還是世界其他地區，該年齡層的腸癌、甲狀腺癌與乳癌病例皆呈現上升趨勢。儘管科學家對於成因已有初步推測，但仍需更多資訊。潛在原因包括現代生活型態的改變、童年時期接觸不同環境因素的影響，以及醫療篩檢普及所帶來的效應。

paragraphs.en: To get a clear picture of the participants' lives, the research team will ask them questions about their education, jobs, where they live, and their general lifestyle. With the permission of the participants, this information will be linked to official health records, such as cancer registries and Medicare, which is Australia’s public health insurance system. Dr. Martin McNamara, the chief executive of the Sax Institute, explained that following people over a long time is necessary. He stated that this method will help experts figure out how to fix and reorganize health and care systems to better serve the population.
paragraphs.zh: 為了清楚掌握參與者的生活狀況，研究團隊將詢問他們關於教育、工作、居住地及一般生活習慣的問題。在取得參與者同意後，這些資訊將與官方健康紀錄連結，例如癌症登記資料以及澳洲的公共健康保險系統「聯邦醫療保險」（Medicare）。薩克斯研究所執行長馬丁·麥克納馬拉（Martin McNamara）博士解釋，長期追蹤民眾是必要的。他表示，這種方法將有助於專家找出如何修正並重組醫療照護體系，以更好地服務大眾。

paragraphs.en: The study is supported by a $4.5 million grant from the National Health and Medical Research Council. Recruitment for the project is scheduled to begin in November. As the participants grow older, the study will change to include age-relevant questions, and it will also adapt to include new health conditions or future pandemics. By gathering this data, the researchers hope to provide the evidence needed to improve the health of future generations.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究獲得「國家健康與醫學研究委員會」（National Health and Medical Research Council）提供的450萬美元補助。計畫招募工作預計於11月開始。隨著參與者年齡增長，研究內容將隨之調整，納入符合年齡層的問題，並會適時調整以涵蓋新的健康狀況或未來的流行病。透過收集這些數據，研究人員希望提供改善未來世代健康所需的實證基礎。

paragraphs.en: This research is important because many current studies only provide a 'snapshot'—a view of health at one specific moment in time. By moving away from this limited approach and tracking people over many years, the Sax Institute hopes to gain a deeper understanding of the complex factors that influence human health. The results could eventually change how doctors treat patients and how governments plan public health policies for years to come.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究之所以重要，是因為目前許多研究僅能提供「快照」——即特定時間點的健康概況。薩克斯研究所希望跳脫這種侷限，透過長達多年的追蹤，深入了解影響人類健康的複雜因素。研究結果最終可能改變醫師治療病患的方式，以及政府未來規劃公共衛生政策的方向。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To use previous achievements or experiences as a base for further development.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於實體建築，這裡指利用過去的經驗來發展新計畫。文中：The new study will build on this experience by looking at how health changes over a person's entire life.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To try to deal with or solve a problem.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（地址），這裡作動詞表示處理問題。文中：One of the main goals of the study is to address the rise in mental health disorders.

keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「修理」物品，這裡指改善醫療系統的運作。文中：He stated that this method will help experts figure out how to fix and reorganize health and care systems to better serve the population.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason researchers are interested in the age group of 18 to 45 for the '18 and Up' study?

options.A: To replace the data collected from the older '45 and Up' study.
options.B: To investigate the increasing prevalence of specific health issues like cancer and mental health problems.
options.C: To test the effectiveness of the current Australian public health insurance system, Medicare.
options.D: To focus exclusively on the impact of childhood environmental exposures on future health.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，該研究旨在探討為何年輕成年人中的心理健康問題及特定癌症變得越來越普遍。選項 A 錯誤，因為該研究是建立在『45 and Up』研究的經驗上，而非取代它；選項 C 錯誤，Medicare 是用來連結資料的工具，而非研究的主要目的；選項 D 錯誤，環境暴露只是研究的其中一小部分，而非針對該年齡層的主要動機。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the '18 and Up' study and the '45 and Up' study?

options.A: They are both managed by the government rather than independent organizations.
options.B: They share the exact same participants to ensure consistency in data.
options.C: The new study benefits from the longitudinal research methods established by the previous one.
options.D: The new study will focus only on the children of the original participants to save time.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。第二段提到 Sax Institute 擁有兩十年的經驗，並透過『45 and Up』研究追蹤年長者，新研究將以此經驗為基礎（build on this experience）來觀察健康如何隨時間變化。選項 A 錯誤，Sax Institute 是非營利組織；選項 B 錯誤，兩者對象年齡層不同；選項 D 錯誤，研究邀請了後代參與，但並非只侷限於此，且研究目的是為了更廣泛的長期追蹤。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'snapshot' mean in the context of the study's methodology?

options.A: A brief, isolated observation of health at a single point in time.
options.B: A high-quality photograph taken for medical records.
options.C: A rapid summary of a patient's entire medical history.
options.D: A sudden change in a person's health status.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到許多現有研究只提供『snapshot』，隨後解釋這指的是『在特定時間點對健康的觀察』，並對比了該研究長期追蹤（tracking people over many years）的方法。選項 B 是字面意思，在文中不適用；選項 C 與 D 則曲解了該詞在比較研究方法時的隱喻意義。

quiz.question: What is the central purpose of the '18 and Up' research project?

options.A: To provide immediate medical treatment for young Australians suffering from cancer.
options.B: To prove that modern lifestyles are the sole cause of early-onset diseases.
options.C: To gather long-term evidence to better understand and address complex health trends in younger generations.
options.D: To collect data that will eventually replace the need for public health insurance systems.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章多次強調該研究是為了獲取長期證據（long-term evidence），以理解影響健康的複雜因素，並改善未來的醫療與政策。選項 A 錯誤，研究旨在提供證據而非直接治療；選項 B 錯誤，文中提到原因尚需研究，並非僅歸咎於生活型態；選項 D 錯誤，文中並未提及要取代保險系統，而是要利用保險資料來協助研究。
